cards.explanation: The reason the song gives is that God's Name is near. It says "we give thanks, for Your Name is near." No long list and no fancy speech, just thanks because God is near, friends. I wish my thank-yous were that clean, because mine usually wander off into a story about my mustache.
The answer is False. The voice says "When I choose a time, I will judge fairly." The voice does the choosing, and it promises to judge fairly. The people don't pick the time, friends.

The answer is that the voice bears up the pillars. In the psalm, the voice says, "When the earth and all its dwellers quake, it is I who bear up its pillars." Everything is shaking, and the voice is the one holding the pillars up. I once rattled one cookie sheet and panicked for an hour, so I respect this, bakers.
The word is "boast." The voice says to the proud, "Do not boast…" Boasting is when you talk yourself up, friends. I've done it over a good batch, and my hat usually bonks something afterward.

The answer is heaven. The voice says, "Do not lift up your horn against heaven or speak with an outstretched neck." Think about that, bakers. Lifting your horn against heaven is aiming way too high. Even I know my limits, and my limit is the top shelf.

The answer is from God who judges. After saying where it doesn't come from, the song says, "…but it is God who judges…" So the source isn't a direction on the map, friends. It's God. No east, no west, no desert, just God. I've been checking every corner of my bakery for the answer to things for years, and it turns out the answer was never in the corner.

The words are "down" and "exalts." The verse says, "He brings down one and exalts another." One gets brought down, and another gets lifted up, because exalts just means lifts up. I've been brought down by a cookie that stuck to the pan, friends, but this is a much bigger deal.

The answer is the wicked. The song says, "…all the wicked of the earth drink it down to the dregs." The cup is in the LORD's hand, and He pours from it. It's the wicked of the earth who drink it, friends.
The answer is False. The song says, "…all the wicked of the earth drink it down to the dregs." That means they drink all the way to the very bottom, bakers. It isn't a quick sip.

The answer is True. After the cup, the song says, "But I will proclaim Him forever…" The word that matters there is forever, friends. That's a long time to keep talking, and I'm the guy who can't stop talking about one batch for ten minutes.

The song ends with the wicked horns cut off and the righteous horns exalted. In the last verse, the voice says, "All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted." The wicked horns get cut off, and the righteous horns get lifted up, friends. It's a clear last line.
